technical_principles.summary: MMA S&C should support repeated high-quality fight actions: strike, defend, shoot, sprawl, clinch, scramble, control, escape, and recover. It should not turn every session into random exhaustion.
Neck, trunk, shoulder, scapular, grip, hip, and posterior-chain capacity matter, but fatiguing these tissues immediately before sparring or hard grappling can reduce protection and skill quality.

MMA requires aerobic recovery plus repeated anaerobic bursts. Conditioning should progress from base intervals and tempo work toward round-based repeat-power only when skill and tissue tolerance are ready.
Sparring, live wrestling, hard grappling, and ground-and-pound exposure should be tracked like training load. Contact intensity, symptoms, sleep, stress, and soreness should influence the next block.

priorities: basic strength across squat, hinge, push, pull, carry, trunk, and unilateral patterns
neck awareness and gentle isometrics when appropriate

avoid_until_ready: stacking all hard stressors on one day
large conditioning spikes while skill quality drops

priorities: performance testing without disrupting skill work
avoid_until_ready: high-intensity work under dehydration or severe fatigue

drills_or_practice_design: scapular push-up and band external rotation
common_errors: using random HIIT as MMA conditioning
doing heavy neck work before sparring
mixing hard sparring, hard wrestling, and heavy strength without recovery planning
ignoring hand, wrist, shoulder, neck, rib, or knee symptoms
turning technical days into exhaustion tests
safety_constraints: Any head symptom blocks contact escalation.
Severe, sharp, worsening, neurological, or persistent pain needs medical review.
Do not prescribe dehydration or weight-cut tactics.
Do not fatigue the neck before contact work.
Reduce impact, grappling, and contact load when sleep, stress, or soreness markers are poor.

sport_training_rules.rule: MMA S&C should support repeatable fight actions instead of creating random fatigue.
recommended_action: Build aerobic base, strength, power, trunk control, shoulder durability, hip mobility, grip endurance, and repeat-power conditioning.
Place high-skill and high-power work before fatigue.
blocked_action: Do not replace MMA conditioning with generic burpee-heavy fatigue circuits.

sport_training_rules.rule: Contact intensity, hard sparring rounds, live wrestling, hard grappling, and symptoms should be tracked as training load.
recommended_action: Bias next session toward technical skill or recovery if symptoms or readiness are poor.
blocked_action: Do not escalate contact after headache, dizziness, visual symptoms, confusion, or worsening neck/head symptoms.

planning_rules.rule: Any headache, dizziness, confusion, visual symptoms, neurological symptoms, or worsening head/neck symptoms blocks sparring and contact escalation.
recommended_action: Use non-contact technical work, mobility, easy aerobic work, or rest.
Recommend medical review for severe, worsening, neurological, or persistent symptoms.

planning_rules.rule: Fight week should reduce fatigue, contact, novelty, and soreness while maintaining timing, sharpness, mobility, and confidence.
recommended_action: Use short technical rounds, reaction primers, mobility, easy aerobic work, and tactical rehearsal.
Avoid new exercises or high-volume lifting.

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Build a physical base for MMA without making skill learning sloppy or unsafe.
progression_signals: keeps technical quality under light fatigue

teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Structure fight-camp preparation around opponent demands, contact load, round simulation, taper, and readiness.
avoid_until_ready: fight camp without stable skill base
progression_signals: can tolerate planned sparring and grappling load
maintains skill quality late in rounds

skill_assessments.summary: Assess whether the athlete can tolerate MMA skill, S&C, and contact load without symptom escalation or skill collapse.

hold_when: headache, dizziness, visual symptoms, confusion, neurological symptoms, or worsening head/neck symptoms
hand, wrist, shoulder, rib, back, hip, knee, or ankle pain worsens
poor sleep, high stress, dehydration, or poor readiness
technical defense breaks down during partner work
level_transition_rules.backend_action: Block contact escalation and bias retrieval toward non-contact skill, mobility, aerobic work, tissue capacity, or rest.
